docs.title: Local AI for Windows apps
docs.text:
CommunityToolkit.AI gives any Windows app, packaged or unpackaged, a small API for local models: chat today, with OCR and speech to text on the way.

using CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat;
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;

ChatModel model = ChatModel.FromCatalog("qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct"); // a handle, no I/O
await model.EnsureReadyAsync(progress);                            // runtime + model, verified
IChatClient client = await model.GetClientAsync();                 // Microsoft.Extensions.AI
ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync("Hello!");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text);

docs.title: Why it is built this way
docs.text:
• Tiny app footprint. Your app references a NuGet package of well under 2 MB. It contains no model code, no ONNX Runtime and no Windows ML.
  • Out-of-process inference. Models run in a separate host process. A model crash never crashes your app; the next call restarts the host.
  • Shared by every app. Apps that use the same model share one host process and one copy of the model on disk.
  • On demand. The runtime and models download the first time an app needs them, into per-user folders, with no elevation.
  • Self-updating. The runtime updates itself without app updates. Your app only speaks a versioned wire contract.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Package What it gives you CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat ChatModel and an IChatClient CommunityToolkit.AI.Ocr OcrModel and OcrClient (preview API; the runtime adapter is in progress) CommunityToolkit.AI.SpeechToText SpeechToTextModel and SpeechToTextClient (preview API; the runtime adapter is in progress) CommunityToolkit.AI.Core Shared by the task packages: Model, status, progress, errors and options

Each task package is versioned on its own, so you can move to a new major version of one task without touching another.

Next: build a console app.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
App process                     Broker (1 per user)               Model hosts (N)
+---------------------+  pipe   +--------------------------+ spawn +----------------------+
| Client library      |<------->| Catalog, store, updater, |<----->| host.exe             |
| API + RPC stub      |         | EP manager, host manager |       | ONNX Runtime GenAI   |
| Bootstrapper        |         +--------------------------+       | task adapter         |
+---------------------+                                            +----------------------+
  • Client libraries (src/Core, src/Chat, ...) contain the API, the bootstrapper and the pipe transport. No model code. Core links the core protocol and trust sources from src/Protocol, so it has no package dependencies.
  • Broker (src/Broker, broker.exe): one per user, singleton by lock file, serving \\.\pipe\LocalAI-<userSid>-v1 with an ACL for the current user only. It resolves the signed catalog, downloads and verifies models, starts hosts, records licences, updates the runtime and idles out after about 10 minutes without clients.
  • Hosts (src/Host, host.exe): one per (model, version, EP, runtime version), shared by every app. Each runs in a kill-on-close job object with memory (and optional CPU) limits, serves sessions over its own current-user-only pipe, schedules requests through a per-model fair queue that favours the foreground app, and exits after 5 idle minutes.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text:
Frames are a 4-byte little-endian length plus a UTF-8 JSON envelope (id, kind, method, payload, error, credits). Fields are additive only and unknown fields are ignored. Streaming results are event frames with credit-based backpressure: the caller grants credits as it consumes, and a slow app pauses generation instead of buffering.

The protocol is layered: the core protocol (handshake, status, acquisition, sessions, errors) and one task contract per task (chat 1.0, ocr 0.1, speech-to-text 0.1), each versioned major.minor. Within a major the lower minor wins. The runtime serves several majors of a task side by side; a client newer than the runtime gets ProtocolTooOld (and triggers an update), a client older than every served major gets NotSupported.

docs.title: Trust
docs.text:
• The release manifest and the catalog are signed with Ed25519. Signing keys are certified by an offline root key that is embedded in the client, separately per purpose (runtime, catalog, models), with revocation in the manifest.
  • Clients refuse a manifest with a lower sequence than the one they saw (anti-rollback) or an expired one (anti-freeze).
  • Every runtime file and every model file is hash-verified before it is executed or mapped. Host adapters ship inside the runtime and are allow-listed; no downloaded code runs.
  • Model downloads are only allowed from hosts in the signed manifest's allow-list, checked on every redirect hop.
  • Per-user installs can be tampered with by malware running as the same user. This is accepted in v1.

docs.title: Not yet implemented
docs.text: These parts of the plan are scheduled for later sprints: Windows ML execution providers (GPU/NPU) and the ExecutionProviderCatalog, the restricted-token / AppContainer host sandbox, the shared-memory data plane for images and audio, the OCR and speech adapters, Authenticode signing, and the C ABI for non-.NET apps.

docs.text:

docs.title: How EnsureReadyAsync works
docs.text: EnsureReadyAsync is idempotent: call it whenever you are about to use a model. When everything is in place it returns in milliseconds.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Connect to the broker. The broker is one process per user that owns downloads, the model store and the model hosts. If it is running, skip to step 4.
  2. Start the installed runtime. If runtime\current.txt points at a runtime whose files verify, start its broker.exe and wait for its pipe.
  3. Install the runtime. Otherwise take the install lock (other apps installing at the same time wait and share the progress), download the signed release manifest from https://andrewleader.github.io/CommunityToolkit.AI/runtime/<channel>/release.json, verify its signature, sequence and expiry, download the runtime zip for this CPU (resumable), verify its hash, extract it safely, verify every file's hash, then point current.txt at it.
  4. Check the model. The broker resolves the id in the signed catalog, checks the task matches, checks hardware, and reports the licence and the bytes to download.
  5. Ask the app. If the licence needs acceptance, your LicenseAcceptance callback runs. Under AcquisitionPolicy.Prompt, your DownloadConsent callback runs. AcquisitionPolicy.Never refuses to download.
  6. Download the model. Every file is downloaded from its revision-pinned Hugging Face URL with resume, verified against the SHA-256 in the signed catalog, stored once by hash, and assembled into the model folder, which is renamed into place only after everything verifies. Several apps asking at once share one download.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text: EnsureProgress has a Stage (Runtime, Ep, Model, Verify), the bytes done and total for that stage, and an OverallFraction from 0 to 1 across all stages, so one progress bar is enough.

docs.title: Where things go
docs.text:
%LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI\
  runtime\<version>\      broker.exe, host.exe and their DLLs, files.json (every hash)
  runtime\current.txt     the active version
  models\<id>\<version>\  model files + model.json
  models\.blobs\          files stored once by SHA-256
  staging\                partial downloads (resumed next time)
  state\                  config, licences, update state, last-known-good
  logs\

docs.title: Sizes
docs.text:
Piece Size Runtime (per architecture) about 50-60 MB download qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct about 1 GB

Disk space is checked before each download, with a safety margin; a shortfall raises InsufficientDiskException.

docs.title: Enterprise settings
docs.text:
Policy values live under HKLM or HKCU \Software\Policies\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI. Machine values win.

Value Type Effect DisableUpdates DWORD 1 The runtime never updates itself. Channel String Pins the update channel, for example stable. RootUrl String Replaces the site root (manifests, catalog, runtime) with an internal mirror of the GitHub Pages site. HuggingFaceMirror String Rewrites https://huggingface.co/ in model URLs to an internal mirror, for networks that block Hugging Face. DisableTelemetry DWORD 1 Turns off telemetry.

Mirrors are safe: the client still verifies every manifest signature and every file hash against the signed catalog, so a mirror can only serve the exact bytes we published.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
The runtime checks for updates every 12-24 hours (with jitter) and on first use after a long idle. A daily per-user scheduled task (CommunityToolkit.AI\LocalAI Updater, no admin) keeps it fresh even when no app runs. A new version is installed side by side, health-checked, then switched to; the old broker drains and exits. If the new version fails to start three times in ten minutes, the runtime rolls back to the last known good version.

Releases use staged rollout percentages and a kill switch in the signed manifest.

docs.title: AppLocker and WDAC
docs.text: The v1 binaries are not Authenticode-signed, so AppLocker and WDAC policies that require signed code block them. This is unsupported until signing ships (see the roadmap).

docs.title: Preview NuGet feed
docs.text:
The packages are published to a static NuGet v3 feed on GitHub Pages until they move to nuget.org.

dotnet nuget add source https://andrewleader.github.io/CommunityToolkit.AI/nuget/v3/index.json -n CommunityToolkit-AI-Preview
dotnet add package CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat --prerelease
  • Versions are prerelease (for example 0.1.0-preview.123), so opt in to prerelease versions.
  • Each package has its own version history. A change that only touches OCR bumps only CommunityToolkit.AI.Ocr.
  • Every published version stays on the feed, so apps pinned to an older version keep restoring.
  • The feed has no search, so browse versions at .../nuget/v3/flatcontainer/<package-id-lowercase>/index.json.
  • GitHub Pages caches for about 10 minutes, so a new version can take a few minutes to appear.

docs.title: Pull request builds
docs.text: Every pull request in this repo publishes its affected packages to its own feed, https://andrewleader.github.io/CommunityToolkit.AI/pr/<number>/nuget/v3/index.json, with versions like 0.1.0-pr42.7. Unchanged packages come from the main feed, so add both sources. The PR's bot comment has the exact commands.

docs.title: Privacy and telemetry
docs.text:
Your content never leaves the device. Prompts, responses, audio and images are processed only by the local model host. They are never logged and never sent anywhere.

Downloads. The runtime downloads manifests, the catalog and runtime packages from andrewleader.github.io (GitHub Pages), and model files from Hugging Face (huggingface.co and its CDN hosts). Like any download, these requests reveal your IP address to GitHub and Hugging Face. Use the enterprise mirror settings to avoid that.

Telemetry is opt-out, minimal and content-free. It records:

  • install and update outcomes and failure codes,
  • model ids and execution provider ids,
  • latency buckets (for example "<2s", never exact timings),
  • host crash counts.

In v1 telemetry is only written locally to logs\telemetry-*.jsonl; there is no upload endpoint yet. Turn it off with the DisableTelemetry policy or by setting the environment variable LOCALAI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1.

docs.title: Quick start: console app (unpackaged)
docs.text:
1. Add the preview feed (see Preview NuGet feed) and the Chat package:

    dotnet nuget add source https://andrewleader.github.io/CommunityToolkit.AI/nuget/v3/index.json -n CommunityToolkit-AI-Preview
dotnet new console -n HelloLocalAI
cd HelloLocalAI
dotnet add package CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat --prerelease

  2. Replace Program.cs. This is the repo's samples/ConsoleChat sample, which CI compiles and runs on every PR:

    using CommunityToolkit.AI;
using CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat;
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;

// Usage: ConsoleChat [model-id] [--prompt "text"] [--yes] [--dev]
//   --prompt  answer one prompt and exit (used by the CI smoke test)
//   --yes     accept the licence and the download without asking
//   --dev     enable dev mode (LOCALAI_DEV_ROOT_URL, LOCALAI_DEV_TRUST_KEY, LOCALAI_HOME, LOCALAI_CHANNEL)
string modelId = args.FirstOrDefault(a => !a.StartsWith("--")) ?? "qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct";
string? oneShot = args.SkipWhile(a => a != "--prompt").Skip(1).FirstOrDefault();
bool yes = args.Contains("--yes");
LocalAIRuntime.EnableDevMode = args.Contains("--dev");
LocalAIRuntime.ClientName = "ConsoleChat";

bool Confirm(string question)
{
    if (yes)
    {
        return true;
    }

    Console.Write($"{question} [y/N] ");
    return Console.ReadLine()?.Trim().Equals("y", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == true;
}

var model = ChatModel.FromCatalog(modelId, new ModelOptions
{
    LicenseAcceptance = (license, _) => ValueTask.FromResult(Confirm($"{license.ModelId} is licensed under {license.LicenseId} ({license.Url}). Accept?")),
    DownloadConsent = (request, _) => ValueTask.FromResult(Confirm($"Download {request.Bytes / (1024.0 * 1024):N0} MB for {request.ModelId}?")),
});

try
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{model.Id}: {await model.GetStatusAsync()}");
    await model.EnsureReadyAsync(new Progress<EnsureProgress>(p =>
        Console.Write($"\r{p.Stage,-8} {p.OverallFraction,6:P0}  {p.BytesDone / (1024.0 * 1024),8:N1} / {p.BytesTotal / (1024.0 * 1024):N1} MB   ")));
    Console.WriteLine();

    IChatClient client = await model.GetClientAsync();
    var history = new List<ChatMessage> { new(ChatRole.System, "You are a helpful assistant. Keep answers short.") };
    while (true)
    {
        string? prompt = oneShot;
        if (prompt is null)
        {
            Console.Write("> ");
            prompt = Console.ReadLine();
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(prompt))
            {
                break;
            }
        }

        history.Add(new ChatMessage(ChatRole.User, prompt));
        string reply = "";
        await foreach (var update in client.GetStreamingResponseAsync(history, new ChatOptions { MaxOutputTokens = 256 }))
        {
            Console.Write(update.Text);
            reply += update.Text;
        }

        Console.WriteLine();
        history.Add(new ChatMessage(ChatRole.Assistant, reply));
        if (oneShot is not null)
        {
            return reply.Length > 0 ? 0 : 1;
        }
    }
}
catch (LocalAiException ex)
{
    Console.Error.WriteLine($"\n{ex.GetType().Name} ({ex.ErrorCode}): {ex.Message}");
    return 1;
}

return 0;

  3. Run it. The first run downloads the runtime (tens of MB) and the model (about 1 GB), asking for licence acceptance and consent first. Later runs start in seconds.

    dotnet run

What happened:

  • ChatModel.FromCatalog created a handle. It did no I/O.
  • EnsureReadyAsync installed the runtime into %LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI, started the per-user broker, and downloaded and verified the model. See How EnsureReadyAsync works.
  • GetClientAsync started (or reused) the shared model host and returned an IChatClient bound to your own session.

docs.title: Quick start: WinUI app (packaged)
docs.text:
Packaged apps use exactly the same API. There is no package identity requirement and no capability to declare: the runtime lives in the user's profile, and the app talks to it over a per-user named pipe.

dotnet add package CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat --prerelease

using CommunityToolkit.AI;
using CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat;
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;

public sealed partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    private readonly ChatModel _model = ChatModel.FromCatalog("qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct", new ModelOptions
    {
        LicenseAcceptance = (license, ct) => ShowLicenseDialogAsync(license, ct),
    });

    private async void OnAskClicked(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
    {
        // Progress is raised on the UI thread because Progress<T> captures the synchronization context.
        var progress = new Progress<EnsureProgress>(p => DownloadBar.Value = p.OverallFraction * 100);
        await _model.EnsureReadyAsync(progress);

        IChatClient client = await _model.GetClientAsync();
        Answer.Text = "";
        await foreach (var update in client.GetStreamingResponseAsync(Question.Text))
        {
            Answer.Text += update.Text;
        }
    }
}

Build your UX from GetStatusAsync(): for example show a "Download model (1 GB)" button when the status is NeedsModel, and go straight to chat when it is Ready. The runtime never shows UI of its own.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Runtime releases are published as GitHub Releases, with notes generated from the merged pull requests.

Package versions are listed on the preview feed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and errors
docs.text: Logs are in %LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI\logs (broker-*.log, host-*.log). They never contain prompts, audio or images.

docs.title: Error reference
docs.text:
Every error derives from LocalAiException and has an ErrorCode.

Exception Code Meaning and what to do NotDownloadedException NotDownloaded The runtime or model is missing and the policy (or the user) did not allow a download. Call EnsureReadyAsync with Prompt or Silent. RuntimeUnavailableException RuntimeUnavailable The runtime could not be installed, started or reached. Check the logs and AV quarantine. DeviceUnsupportedException DeviceUnsupported No available device can run the model (memory or execution provider). ModelUnknownException ModelUnknown The id is not in the catalog, or it is not a model for this task. HostCrashedException HostCrashed The model host crashed. Retry: the next call restarts it. BusyException Busy The runtime is overloaded. Retry later. LicenseNotAcceptedException LicenseNotAccepted Set ModelOptions.LicenseAcceptance and let the user accept. NotSupportedByRuntimeException NotSupported The peer does not support this operation or contract version. ProtocolTooOldException ProtocolTooOld Your package needs a newer runtime. The runtime has been asked to update; retry shortly. OfflineException Offline A download failed because the network is unavailable. Downloads resume when you retry. InsufficientDiskException InsufficientDisk Free up disk space. LocalAiException IntegrityFailure A downloaded file or manifest failed verification and was discarded.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Antivirus quarantined broker.exe or host.exe. v1 binaries are unsigned and the runtime self-updates over a named pipe, which some AV products flag. Restore the file or allow-list %LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI\runtime; the next EnsureReadyAsync re-verifies and repairs the install.

Proxy or captive portal. Downloads use the system proxy. A captive portal shows up as a signature or hash failure (the portal's page is not our file) and nothing is installed. Sign in to the network and retry.

Corporate network blocks Hugging Face. Set the HuggingFaceMirror policy (see Enterprise settings).

Low disk space. The runtime needs about 200 MB free; a model needs its size plus 10%.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
The runtime is per user and has a visible uninstall:

  • Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Local AI Runtime (CommunityToolkit.AI) > Uninstall, or
  • run %LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI\runtime\localai.cmd --uninstall.

Uninstall stops the broker and every model host, removes the scheduled update task and the Apps entry, and deletes the runtime, models, downloads, state and logs.

Apps that use the runtime install it again the next time they call EnsureReadyAsync.

To remove only models, delete folders under %LocalAppData%\CommunityToolkit\LocalAI\models while no app is using them; the runtime also removes superseded model versions on its own.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text: CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat exposes local chat models through Microsoft.Extensions.AI's IChatClient, so code written against IChatClient (including middleware such as logging or caching) works unchanged.

docs.title: Get a client
docs.text:
var model = ChatModel.FromCatalog("qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct", new ModelOptions
{
    Device = Device.Auto,                       // a preference; the runtime falls back
    AcquisitionPolicy = AcquisitionPolicy.Prompt,
    LicenseAcceptance = (license, ct) => AskUserAsync(license, ct),
    DownloadConsent = (request, ct) => AskUserAsync($"Download {request.Bytes / 1_000_000} MB?", ct),
});

await model.EnsureReadyAsync(progress);
IChatClient client = await model.GetClientAsync(new ChatClientOptions { DefaultMaxOutputTokens = 512 });

docs.title: Single response or streaming
docs.text:
ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync("Summarize this in one line: ...");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text);
Console.WriteLine(response.Usage?.OutputTokenCount);

await foreach (ChatResponseUpdate update in client.GetStreamingResponseAsync(history))
{
    Console.Write(update.Text);
}

docs.title: Options
docs.text: ChatOptions Supported MaxOutputTokens Yes. FinishReason is Length when the limit is hit. Temperature, TopP, TopK, Seed Yes. Without them, decoding is greedy. StopSequences Yes, up to 16. Instructions Yes, sent as a system message. Tools / function calling Not yet.

docs.title: Sessions and the KV cache
docs.text: Each IChatClient is its own session in the shared host, and nothing is shared across apps. Within a session, the host keeps the model's KV cache between turns: when you send the conversation again with a new user message, only the new tokens are processed. Up to four sessions per model keep a cache; older ones are rebuilt on their next turn.

docs.title: Cancellation and crashes
docs.text: Cancelling the token stops generation in the host. If the host process crashes, in-flight calls raise HostCrashedException, and the next call on the same client restarts the host automatically.

docs.title: Migration guides
docs.text: CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat 1.x speaks chat contract 1.x. When a 2.0 ships, its migration guide will be listed here, and the runtime keeps serving 1.x for 12 months after that.

docs.title: OCR
docs.text:
Preview

The CommunityToolkit.AI.Ocr API and its task contract (0.1) are published so apps can start building against them. The runtime's OCR adapter and the shared-memory data plane land in sprint 7, and no OCR model is in the catalog yet. Until then EnsureReadyAsync raises ModelUnknownException for OCR ids.

using CommunityToolkit.AI.Ocr;

var model = OcrModel.FromCatalog("<ocr-model-id>");
await model.EnsureReadyAsync();
await using OcrClient client = await model.GetClientAsync();

await using var image = File.OpenRead("receipt.png");
OcrResult result = await client.RecognizeAsync(image, new OcrOptions { Language = "en-US" });
foreach (OcrLine line in result.Lines)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{line.Text} at {line.Bounds}");
}

Input and result types (OcrResult, OcrLine, OcrBounds) belong to this package; they are not shared with other tasks.

docs.title: Speech to text
docs.text:
Preview

The CommunityToolkit.AI.SpeechToText API and its task contract (0.1) are published so apps can start building against them. The Whisper adapter lands in sprint 8, and no speech model is in the catalog yet.

using CommunityToolkit.AI.SpeechToText;

var model = SpeechToTextModel.FromCatalog("<speech-model-id>");
await model.EnsureReadyAsync();
await using SpeechToTextClient client = await model.GetClientAsync();

await using var wav = File.OpenRead("meeting.wav"); // 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM
await foreach (TranscriptSegment segment in client.TranscribeStreamingAsync(wav))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{segment.Start:mm\\:ss}] {segment.Text}");
}

docs.title: Adding a model
docs.text: Model files stay on Hugging Face. A catalog entry pins a commit and records every file's size and SHA-256, and the client verifies every byte against our signed catalog before the host maps it.

docs.title: 1. Pick a repo
docs.text:
• Prefer publisher-provided ONNX repos in the ONNX Runtime GenAI layout (genai_config.json next to the model).
  • The repo must be public and not gated: files must download anonymously.
  • Review the licence for redistribution and use terms. We link to the files rather than redistributing them, but the licence still applies to the user.

docs.title: 2. Generate the entry
docs.text:
dotnet run --project tools/LocalAI.Tools -- catalog add <owner>/<repo> <revision> `
  --include <subfolder>/ --id <catalog-id> --task chat --adapter ort-genai-chat `
  --license-id <SPDX id> --license-url <url> --display-name "<name>" --min-memory-mb 4096 --eps cpu `
  --param maxLength=4096

catalog add resolves the revision to a commit sha, lists the files, takes the SHA-256 of LFS files from the Hugging Face API (and downloads and hashes small non-LFS files), and writes catalog/models/<id>.json with revision-pinned URLs (never main).

Use --hidden to ship an entry dark: it then resolves only for dev-mode clients.

Adapter parameters for ort-genai-chat: maxLength (context length per session, default 4096), maxCachedSessions (sessions that keep a KV cache, default 4), chatTemplate (overrides the model's template), subfolder.

docs.title: 3. Open a PR
docs.text:
CI checks every changed entry: the URLs are revision-pinned, the repo is public and ungated, sizes and hashes match the Hugging Face metadata, the files download anonymously, and the licence is recorded. The PR's staging catalog overlays production with your entry, so you can try it right away from the staging site.

A scheduled job re-checks every URL daily (and every hash weekly) and opens an issue if a file or repo moves.

docs.title: Current models
docs.text:
qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct uses khanuckaeff/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Olive-Onnx (cpu_and_mobile), an int4 community conversion of Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Apache-2.0). Qwen does not publish a GenAI-format ONNX build, and the onnx-community builds target Transformers.js rather than GenAI. Replacing it with a publisher-provided build (or our own conversion, which would mean hosting files ourselves) is an open decision.

test-echo is the hidden smoke-test model. Its single tiny file exists only so the whole acquisition path runs; the test-echo adapter replies with an echo.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
Key Where it lives Used for Root Offline (never on a CI machine). Its public key is embedded in every client and runtime (src/Protocol/Trust/TrustRoots.cs). Certifying signing keys. Runtime signing key GitHub Environment preview-signing (RUNTIME_SIGNING_KEY, RUNTIME_SIGNING_CERT) runtime/preview/release.json Release key GitHub Environment release, with required reviewers (RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY, RELEASE_SIGNING_CERT) runtime/stable/release.json Catalog signing key GitHub Environment preview-signing (CATALOG_SIGNING_KEY, CATALOG_SIGNING_CERT) catalog/catalog.json Models key Reserved for signing model metadata when we host files ourselves. — Staging key Generated per PR run, trusted only in dev mode PR staging sites

A certificate binds a signing key to the root for a set of purposes and an expiry. A runtime key cannot sign a catalog, and the reverse. PR workflows never see the production keys, and fork PRs get no secrets at all.

docs.title: Creating the production keys
docs.text:
dotnet run --project tools/LocalAI.Tools -- keygen --out <offline-folder> --valid-days 730

This writes root.key / root.pub and a key plus certificate per purpose. Then:

  1. Put root.pub into TrustRoots.Production.
  2. Store each *.key file's contents and each *.cert.json file's contents as the environment secrets above.

  3. Certify a separate release key for the stable channel:

    dotnet run --project tools/LocalAI.Tools -- certify --root-key <offline-folder>/root.key `
  --public-key <release public key> --purposes runtime --valid-days 365 --out release.cert.json

  4. Move root.key offline (for example to a hardware-backed vault), and delete every other copy.

docs.title: Rotation and revocation
docs.text:
• Rotate a signing key: generate a new key, certify it with the root, update the secrets. Old manifests stay valid until they expire.
  • Revoke a key: publish a manifest with --revoked-keys <keyId>. Clients stop trusting anything signed by that key, including catalogs.
  • Rotate the root: add the new root's public key to TrustRoots.Production next to the old one, ship clients and runtimes, then start certifying with the new root and revoke the old root's id.

docs.title: Anti-rollback and anti-freeze
docs.text: Every manifest and catalog has a monotonic sequence and an expires time. Clients remember the highest sequence they have seen per document and refuse anything older or expired. The scheduled workflow re-signs the preview manifest and the catalog daily so they never expire; stable manifests last 90 days and the scheduled check opens an issue when one expires within 7 days.

docs.title: Build and test
docs.text:
dotnet build CommunityToolkit.AI.slnx
dotnet test tests/CommunityToolkit.AI.Protocol.Tests   # framing, RPC, Ed25519 (RFC 8032), manifests, zip safety, downloads
dotnet test tests/CommunityToolkit.AI.Runtime.Tests    # end to end: packages -> bootstrapper -> broker -> host

The end-to-end tests pack this repo's broker and host into a runtime zip, sign a local site with throwaway keys, serve it on 127.0.0.1, and drive the public API in dev mode. Each test uses its own install home under %TEMP%, so they never touch your real install. They cover first run, licence and consent, sharing one host, crash recovery, cancellation, integrity failures, concurrent installs and a side-by-side self-update.

docs.title: Run the sample against a local site
docs.text:
tools/dev-site.ps1 builds a complete signed site with dev keys, using the same localai-tools commands CI uses:

./tools/dev-site.ps1            # prints the four environment variables to set
$env:LOCALAI_DEV_ROOT_URL  = '...'
$env:LOCALAI_DEV_TRUST_KEY = '...'
$env:LOCALAI_CHANNEL       = 'local'
$env:LOCALAI_HOME          = '...'
dotnet run --project samples/ConsoleChat -- test-echo --dev --yes --prompt "hello"
dotnet run --project samples/ConsoleChat -- qwen-2.5-1.5b-instruct --dev --yes

The site is read through file:// by default; add -Serve to serve it on http://127.0.0.1:8787/ instead.

docs.title: Dev mode
docs.text:
Dev mode lets a client trust a non-production root URL and key. It is enabled when the app sets LocalAIRuntime.EnableDevMode = true (it is on by default only in Debug builds of Core). Environment variables alone cannot enable it in a release build, so they cannot redirect a shipping app.

Variable Meaning LOCALAI_DEV_ROOT_URL Site root (https, http://127.0.0.1, or file://). LOCALAI_DEV_TRUST_KEY Extra root public keys (base64, comma-separated). LOCALAI_CHANNEL Channel, for example pr-42. LOCALAI_HOME Install home. Kernel object names get a suffix so this never collides with the real install.

Runtime tuning knobs, read by the broker and hosts: LOCALAI_BROKER_IDLE_SECONDS, LOCALAI_HOST_IDLE_SECONDS, LOCALAI_HOST_MEMORY_MB, LOCALAI_HOST_CPU_PERCENT, LOCALAI_UPDATE_INITIAL_DELAY_SECONDS, LOCALAI_UPDATE_INTERVAL_SECONDS, LOCALAI_LOG_CONSOLE=1, LOCALAI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1.

docs.text:
src/Core           CommunityToolkit.AI.Core (transport, bootstrapper, Model base)
src/Chat           CommunityToolkit.AI.Chat

docs.title: CI, staging and releases
docs.text: Workflow Trigger What it does ci.yml called by the others Build, protocol and end-to-end tests on x64 and ARM64, pack, size gates, self-contained runtime zips, catalog checks, docs build, spell and link checks. pr.yml every PR CI, then for same-repo PRs: stage pr/<n>/ (docs, feed with affected packages, runtime manifest on channel pr-<n> signed with an ephemeral key, catalog overlay), a smoke test on a clean Windows runner, and a PR comment with links. pr-cleanup.yml PR closed Removes pr/<n>/. preview.yml push to main CI, then publishes the preview channel to the site root: docs, feed (all old versions kept), runtime, catalog. release.yml manual, release environment with reviewers Promotes the preview manifest to stable (re-signed with the release key), with rollout percent, kill switch and min version. Creates a GitHub Release with generated notes. scheduled.yml daily Verifies the live site, checks every catalog URL (full hashes weekly), re-signs preview manifests and the catalog, removes stale PR staging folders.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Each package is versioned independently with MinVer and a per-package tag prefix: core-v, chat-v, ocr-v, stt-v. Tag chat-v1.0.0 to release Chat 1.0.0. Between tags, versions are prereleases: -preview.<run> from main and -pr<n>.<run> from PRs. localai-tools affected maps changed paths to packages: a change to src/Core, the core protocol, trust code or build files affects every package; a task folder affects only that package. Only affected packages are published to a PR's feed.

Task packages depend on Core with the range [x.y.z, 2.0.0).

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
The site is the gh-pages branch, rewritten as one orphan commit on every deploy so binaries never pile up in history. Deploys share one concurrency group. The deploy action prunes runtime versions that no channel references (keeping the newest two) and fails if the site would exceed 950 MB.

Smoke tests read the staged site through file:// (the same bytes that were deployed), because Pages caches for about 10 minutes.

docs.title: Rolling back
docs.text: Promotion is a manifest change, so rollback is too: run release.yml with source set to an older manifest, or set kill-switch to the bad version (clients on it update to the manifest's version). A runtime that crash-loops on a machine rolls back to the last known good version on its own.
